Engine-level with zero product coupling.","maintainers":[{"name":"brainbotbrain","email":"denissutherland@gmail.com"}],"readme":"# @gridlock/kernel

Generic agent-based modelling substrate for gridlock games — deterministic
schedulers, a graph-space environment, event emission, and the ledger /
journal / taxonomy / narrative / social layers built on top.

Engine-level with zero product coupling: the kernel knows about agents,
ticks and events, and nothing about what any particular game's agents
*are*. Hosts wire it to a product through adapters, not subclassing.

Zero runtime dependencies.

## What you get

| Symbol | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Model`, `ModelConfig` | The simulation container — holds agents, space and bus, and drives ticks. |
| `RandomScheduler`, `SimultaneousScheduler`, `FixedOrderScheduler` | Tick ordering policies. Determinism comes from the injected `Rng`, so a seeded run replays exactly. |
| `createRng`, `Rng` | Seeded PRNG. Every stochastic decision in the kernel draws from it. |
| `GraphSpace` | Graph-structured environment — nodes, edges, agent placement and neighbourhood queries. |
| `EventBus`, `EventSubscriber` | In-process event emission for the tick loop. |
| `Ledger`, `LedgerSnapshot`, `LedgerQuery`, `ObserverScope` | Append-only, replayable, observer-scoped view over the bus. Adds what the raw bus lacks: a serialization boundary for cross-session replay, structured queries (by actor, kind, tick range), and scoping — what a given observer is allowed to have seen. |
| `Journal`, `JournalEntry`, `JournalConfig` | Entry-typed **player** journal — player-authored records of their own reasoning, explicitly *not* system truth. Vocabulary-neutral: products register their own entry types, statuses and transition rules. |
| Taxonomy: `MOVEMENT`, `COMMUNICATION`, `MEETING`, `TRANSFER`, `RELATIONSHIP` + `movementEvent(…)` etc. + `isMovement(…)` etc. | A shared five-kind event vocabulary with constructors and type guards, so downstream layers can reason about events without a per-game schema. |
| `salience`, `topHighlights`, `buildTimeline`, `firedStorylets`, `detectAnomalies` | Narrative projection — scoring which events matter, assembling timelines, and flagging outliers. |
| `SocialState`, `SocialGraph`, `createCharacterState` | Relationship, memory, motive and faction state between agents. |
| `createProjection`, `createCompositeProjection`, `ProjectionRegistry` | Workspace projections — filtered/transformed views of kernel state for a host UI. |

## Installation

```bash
npm install @gridlock/kernel
```

## Status

Pre-1.0 (`0.1.x`). The engine is developed inside a private monorepo and
published from there; there is no public issue tracker or support
commitment. See the `@gridlock` org on npm for the rest of the packages.

MIT licensed.
